requirements.requirement: node1's link to node2 (eth1) is placed in its own VLAN as an untagged/access port
requirements.summary: SONiC's `config vlan` CLI rejected eth1/eth2 because they are not registered Ethernet* front-panel ports in this virtualized topology (cmd-6bdec664c52e42a8, cmd-7e97179d54ba42e1). The executor instead built a vlan_filtering Linux bridge (br0) on node1 and set eth1 as PVID/untagged member of VLAN 10 (cmd-076416d989a843a3), directly confirmed by `bridge vlan show` output showing 'eth1 10 PVID Egress Untagged' (cmd-27e5e2b777ca419b, cmd-bcb254329cb94e31). This is a reasonable, directly-observed equivalent implementation given the platform's CLI limitation.

requirements.requirement: node1's link to node3 (eth2) is placed in its own, different VLAN as an untagged/access port
requirements.summary: Same bridge build assigned eth2 as PVID/untagged member of a separate VLAN 20, confirmed by the same `bridge vlan show` output ('eth2 20 PVID Egress Untagged').

requirements.requirement: Each host (node2, node3) keeps a working link to node1 inside its own VLAN
requirements.summary: node2 (192.168.10.2) successfully pings node1's VLAN10 interface (192.168.10.1) with 0% loss (cmd-04690e2c8f184c77); node3 (192.168.20.2) successfully pings node1's VLAN20 interface (192.168.20.1) with 0% loss (cmd-6900a79ef1874036). Directly observed, not just claimed.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 stay separated from one another (cross-VLAN isolation)
requirements.summary: node2 could not reach either 192.168.20.1 (node1's VLAN20 side) or 192.168.20.2 (node3), 100% packet loss both ways; node3 symmetrically could not reach VLAN10 addresses, 100% packet loss (cmd-04690e2c8f184c77, cmd-6900a79ef1874036). Bridge VLAN/FDB tables directly confirm eth1 and eth2 are in disjoint VLANs 10/20 with no shared membership (cmd-bcb254329cb94e31).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — per-host VLAN segmentation on node1 as untagged access ports, working per-VLAN links to node1, and cross-VLAN isolation between node2 and node3 — are directly demonstrated via ping and bridge-table evidence, both before and after the mandatory restart-evidence protocol. Because SONiC-VS's `config vlan` CLI does not recognize the virtio data-plane NICs (eth1/eth2), the executor substituted a vlan_filtering Linux bridge as an equivalent access-port mechanism; this is a reasonable implementation choice given the platform constraint and is directly verified, not merely claimed. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed for all three nodes with directly observed pre/post boot-ID changes and disruption, but node1's bridge/VLAN configuration does not persist across reboot and had to be manually rebuilt by the executor post-restart — recovery was demonstrated but not automatic, which is a limitation on the durability of the solution rather than a failure of the stated task (which does not require reboot persistence).
limitations: node1's bridge-based VLAN configuration (br0, br0.10, br0.20, docker0 changes) does not persist across reboot on this SONiC-VS image; post-restart 'recovery' required the executor to manually re-run the same configuration commands rather than the system self-healing, so no automatic persistence mechanism (e.g. a boot-time script or systemd unit) was put in place.

The task's implied SONiC-native VLAN CLI mechanism (`config vlan member add ... -u`) could not be used because eth1/eth2 are not registered Ethernet* ports in this virtualized topology; the executor's Linux-bridge substitute achieves the same functional outcome but is a different implementation layer than a native SONiC VLAN would use.

Command timeline is available and largely unambiguous, but some intermediate `config vlan add 10/20` command outputs were not fully captured, so exact confirmation that no residual empty VLAN entries were left in the config DB relies on the subsequent redis-cli check rather than direct output of the delete commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: One bounded troubleshooting mutation occurred and was fully reverted: the executor ran `config vlan add 10`/`config vlan add 20` (cmd-7e97179d54ba42e1) which likely created empty VLAN entries in the SONiC config DB when the CLI accepted the VLAN IDs but rejected the eth1/eth2 port members; the executor then attempted cleanup with `config vlan del 10/20` (cmd-94672957e7c844b2) and verified via `redis-cli -n 4 keys VLAN*` that the VLAN config DB was empty afterward (cmd-8ca53d4ba596496f), confirming no residue. The docker0 class-E IP removal (cmd-6bdec664c52e42a8) is a persistent mutation but was described as a documented step from the SONiC reference runbook and did not conflict with any task-relevant service. No abandoned files, conflicting services, or unsafe exposure were introduced by the executor; the two pre-existing failed systemd units (system-health.service, watchdog-control.service) on node1 are present in both before_prepare and after_executor snapshots and are not executor-caused.
